business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national legal order with hybrid EU-law influences)

Double Taxation Agreements of Luxembourg (including with France, Germany, the Netherlands, the United States and the People's Republic of China)
EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (trade and investment framework applicable to Luxembourg)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI) as applied to Luxembourg DTAAs
EU bilateral free trade and investment protection agreements extending to Luxembourg

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 180 to 205 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarised deed of incorporation) together with the coordinated articles of association, submitted electronically by the Luxembourg notary to the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum issued and fully paid-up share capital, fully subscribed at incorporation; the capital must be deposited in a blocked bank account opened in the name of the company in formation, with the bank's blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) produced to the notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [S.à r.l.] RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscription to its entire issued share capital, set at EUR 12,000, all contributions having been deposited in the incorporation bank account and evidenced by the banker's certificate; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [•], Luxembourg, and the manager is authorised to take on lease the premises and to exercise all corporate rights; RESOLVED, that [•] is appointed as manager (gérant) with general management powers and [•] as approved signatory, with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete all statutory, tax and licensing registrations. All resolutions are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online name search and reservation facility.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS and trademark databases for identical or confusingly similar names; submit an application to reserve the proposed name for a short period; ensure the legal entity form designation 'S.à r.l.' is included in the corporate name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name
Identification details of the incorporator(s)
Authorised share capital information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or objected to, select a distinctive alternative name, recertify availability, and resubmit the reservation application; if a trademark opposition is raised, obtain a consent letter from the prior right holder or proceed with a modified name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Incorporation Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, Société Générale Luxembourg, BGL BNP Paribas) or another EU bank accepted by Luxembourg banking practice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of '[Name] SARL en formation'; deposit the full minimum share capital of EUR 12,000; instruct the bank to issue an attestation de blocage confirming that the capital is blocked and held in the company's name pending RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Valid passport or national identity card of each shareholder and manager
Proof of residential address
Source of funds declaration and bank statements
Brief business plan and expected activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced KYC documentation, promptly deliver source-of-wealth evidence, tax references from the home country, or a corporate structure chart; if the bank refuses the account, apply at an alternative Luxembourg credit institution and maintain continuity of the notarial timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Maître de droit luxembourgeois appointed under the Law of 9 August 1999 on notaries).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the draft articles of association and bank blocking certificate to the notary; review and sign the deed of incorporation before the notary, together with corporate governance schedules; the notary authenticates the deed and transmits it electronically to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage)
Draft articles of association
Valid identification and passport copies of shareholders and managers
No criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) from country of residence for managers
Notarised power of attorney if a representative signs on behalf of a shareholder
Registered office lease or head-office authorisation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests amendments to the articles or attachment of additional declarations, implement the amendments, arrange re-signature of the deed, and re-execute the notarial protocol; if a shareholder is unable to appear, execute a specific power of attorney and have it legalised or apostilled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice online filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the signed deed and corporate documents electronically with the RCS; pay the official RCS filing fee; RCS reviews the file, assigns the registration number, and publishes an excerpt in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); the company acquires legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Executed notarial deed of incorporation
Banking certificate of blocked capital
Statement of legality and conformity signed by the notary
Identification and declarations of the manager(s)
Registered office acceptance and lease details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or requests supplementary documents, the notary supplements the dossier online, corrects formal defects, and re-files; if the query concerns the manager's capacity or background, provide certified translations of criminal records or professional declarations within the RCS deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security and Business License Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes; municipal authority of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, register for Luxembourg VAT (numéro de TVA), register as employer with the CCSS, and apply for the autorisation d'établissement (business establishment licence) under the Law of 2 September 2011; simultaneously submit the environmental classified-establishment declaration and municipal operating permit as required for the food-and-beverage service.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and registration number
Notarial deed and articles of association
Statutory declaration of good repute and absence of bankruptcy
Professional qualifications or evidence of management competence
Lease agreement and floor plan of the tea salon
Fire safety certificate and environmental declaration form
Details of the VAT tax advisor or accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority challenges professional qualifications, submit recognised diplomas or undertake a complementary training module; if the municipality raises zoning or safety objections, adjust the premises portfolio, submit an amended layout plan, and obtain a revised fire-prevention certificate; appeal any refusal before the administrative tribunal within the statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Artisans (Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes, DGCM) together with the municipal authorities of the commune where the tea salon is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Licence) for food and beverage serving activities under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to professions and the exercise of services, supplemented by the communal commercial operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency, Luxembourg Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Simple Declaration (Établissements Classés) under the Law of 9 May 2014 on classified establishments; a small-scale tea salon/lounge with fewer than 200 seats and a floor area below 1,000 m² is generally exempt from a full EIA, but must file an environmental declaration with the commune.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must meet municipal sewerage discharge limits (pH 6.5–9.5, COD/BOD5 thresholds set by the local concession); kitchen exhausts must comply with ventilation and VOC odour-control standards; waste grease and food waste must be separately collected by licensed waste operators in accordance with Luxembourg waste management regulations; all surface-water protection requirements of the EU Water Framework Directive apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance evidenced by a certificate from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) or communal fire service; structural and building safety approval from the municipal building authority; workplace health-and-safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering electrical safety, emergency exits, ventilation, and occupational risk assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg direct tax administration — and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — VAT, registration and excise duties. Unified portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu/en.html).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For foreign founders establishing an SARL in Luxembourg: (1) complete incorporation with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) through MyGuichet, obtaining the 8-digit national matricule; (2) apply for VAT using AEDT Form 604 or eTVA online application, with non-established foreign suppliers appointing a Luxembourg tax representative when no permanent establishment exists; (3) the VAT ID is issued in the format 'LU' followed by 8 digits; the same national number serves as the statutory TIN for corporate income, municipal business and net wealth tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg domestic tax law does not provide a check-the-box election for SARLs: an SARL is a per se taxable corporation resulting in CIT/MBT/NWT exposure with no pass-through option. Available elections include VAT grouping (assujetti unique) for economically/financially linked persons and fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for 95%+ resident group losses/income. Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD) apply; only specific structured arrangement timing elections are possible and no elective classification for legal form is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) under the Luxembourg small-business exemption; EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold for distance sales of goods/e-services; non-established suppliers generally must register for Luxembourg VAT when making taxable supplies unless reverse charge or customer self-assessment applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate exists in Luxembourg for B2B/B2C retail. E-invoicing is permitted where authenticity, integrity and legibility are guaranteed; B2G invoices must be transmitted via a PEPPOL-compliant platform under EU Directive 2014/55/EU. Luxembourg VAT returns are submitted periodically through the eTVA/MyGuichet portal with no government pre-clearance of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) is available for physical exports of goods to destinations outside the EU where the supplier retains evidence of dispatch/transportation within the applicable deadline (generally one month after supply). Intra-EU dispatches to a valid EU VAT number may be zero-rated/exempt subject to correct reporting. Services supplied to non-EU customers are normally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under place-of-supply rules. On-premises tea salon and lounge services delivered in Luxembourg are taxable at the reduced sit-down rate and are not eligible for export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/NCTS export declaration through Luxembourg Customs)
Transport Document (CMR, Bill of Lading or Air Waybill) evidencing movement from Luxembourg to the non-EU destination
Proof of physical exit from the EU (customs validation or destination customs entry stamp)
Proof of payment for the export supply (e.g. bank credit advice, SWIFT/MT103)
Inward remittance/foreign currency receipt evidence to substantiate payment repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax and customs authorities may conduct retrospective audits of export substantiation. Failure to provide complete statutory evidence invalidates zero-rating, and VAT becomes due with default interest (monthly late-payment interest), administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 per infringement, and, in fraud cases, criminal penalties including additional fines and imprisonment. Wrongly claimed input VAT or zero-rated export treatment is clawed back with statutory interest from the original filing date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent prudential and foreign exchange operations supervisor within the Eurosystem.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full capital and current account convertibility as a member of the EU and the Eurozone, consistent with OECD and IMF Article VIII obligations. No foreign exchange controls restrict currency conversion or transfers for the SARL's capital contribution, profit repatriation, dividend distribution, or operational settlements. Dividend distributions are subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at 15% under domestic law, but may be reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or 5% / 0% under applicable double tax treaties, provided corporate substance, beneficial ownership, and compliance with anti-abuse provisions are satisfied. Cross-border payments above EUR 12,500 must be reported for balance-of-payments statistics by the ordering bank or the reporting institution to the BCL, but this is a statistical and monitoring mechanism, not a restrictive control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory obligation exists to surrender, repatriate, or mandatorily convert export proceeds into EUR within a specified timeline. Luxembourg law adheres to EU free movement of capital principles, allowing the Specialty Tea Salon Lounge to hold foreign currency proceeds offshore or in domestic multi-currency accounts, provided underlying transactions are bona fide and anti-money laundering record-keeping requirements are met. Banks may require commercial invoices and shipping documents to validate export flows, but there is no legal conversion ratio or surrender deadline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for SARL registered capital deposit; Operational Account for daily treasury and POS/card settlement
Escrowed Share Capital Account under notarial deed; Operational EUR and multi-currency accounts, Commercial LC issuance facility
Capital Subscription Account and Operational Merchant Services Account with integrated cross-border payment rails

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE - Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Public-sector-friendly operational and escrow accounts, particularly suitable for local VAT and social security clearing

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Quintet Private Bank (formerly KBL European Private Bankers)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Premium operational account with dedicated relationship manager for UHNW-linked shareholders, limited merchant acquiring
Operational account and wealth-linked treasury services for founder-owned SARLs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility for offshore, non-EU digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) was assessed as LOW due to absence of a Luxembourg or EU authorisation and the failure to qualify for passporting. EU/EEA-licensed EMIs operating under PSD2 (e.g., established in Lithuania, Ireland, or the Netherlands) may provide ancillary payment accounts and card issuance through EEA passport notification to the CSSF; however, they cannot act as the SARL's primary settlement bank for commercial deposit-taking, trade finance, or escrow of statutory share capital. The thematic cash management account must ultimately be held with a fully-fledged credit institution established or passported in Luxembourg to ensure regulatory protection, insolvency ring-fencing, and integration with SEPA / TARGET2.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, at least one natural person who is a duly authorised director (gérant) or a senior officer of the SARL must attend an initial in-person KYC identity verification at the selected bank's office in Luxembourg. Remote onboarding via secure video identification is legally permissible under CSSF AML/CTF guidelines for low-risk entities where all shareholders and managers hold EU/EEA or OECD passports and the corporate structure is transparent, but many tier-1 domestic banks still require physical appearance for the first account opening and prior to activating the Capital Escrow Account. All ultimate beneficial owners holding more than 25% of shares or control must submit identity documents and proof of address; powers of attorney must be notarised and apostilled if signed outside Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner is a politically exposed person (PEP) or is resident in a high-risk third country listed by FATF / EU Commission.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive dossier including formal PEP risk assessment by the Luxembourg registered agent; source of wealth and source of funds documentation with authenticated bank references; valid passport, tax residence certificate, and proof of the owner's legitimate business history; notarised explanation of the underlying investment rationale; commitment to transactional limits; enhanced ongoing monitoring acceptance letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex and multi-layered corporate ownership structure, especially involving trusts, foundations, or offshore Delaware / BVI holding layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date corporate organisation chart signed by the gérant; registration extracts from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and equivalent foreign registries; Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing confirmation; legal opinion from a Luxembourg counsel confirming the economic substance and absence of artificiality; board resolutions approving the account opening; certified constitutional documents and bank references for each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High proportion of cash transactions from on-premises tea salon operations, creating perceived money-laundering or tax-evasion risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business model narrative describing the Specialty Tea Salon Lounge format; monthly projected cash and card turnover split from the business plan; installed cashier system with tamper-proof cash reconciliation; point-of-sale merchant contract and complaint-handling procedures; Luxembourg VAT registration certificate and output VAT remittance history; internal cash management policy with daily deposit limits; evidence of employee background checks and training records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from a non-EU jurisdiction into the Capital Escrow Account in a single tranche.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share subscription and deed of contribution to the SARL; evidence of funds provenance (e.g., sale agreement of assets, shareholder savings statements, corporate resolution of investing parent); source of funds documentation covering the last 12 months; international wire transfer instruction showing incoming beneficiary name and purpose code; tax identification of the transferring entity; confirmations of no UBO sanctions or adverse media from a commercial screening database; legal advice note on the commercial substance of the cross-border investment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder loan injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 (single payment) or MT202 (bank-to-bank cover) in EUR to the SARL's EUR account at a Luxembourg credit institution, with a purpose code aligned to BPM6 / ECB statistics. For equity capital subscription, use the purpose code 'S0102' (Investment in capital of non-financial corporations) or equivalent BCL statistical purpose code; for shareholder loans use 'S0101' (Investment in debt of non-financial corporations). The sending bank must reference the beneficiary account name exactly as per RCS, include the ISIN or RCS number, and provide underlying evidence (signed subscription agreements, notarised deed, bank reference) to the receiving Luxembourg bank. For amounts above EUR 50,000, the Luxembourg bank will file the mandatory balance-of-payments report with the BCL within the statutory deadline, but no exchange-control approval is required. A bank confirmation of receipt can also serve as the statutory capital certificate (attestation bancaire) required to register the SARL with the RCS and before a notary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for specialty tea imports and ceramic salon inventories shall primarily use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers in EUR or major currencies, and for high-value or first-time vendor relationships, commercial letters of credit (LC) issued by the Luxembourg bank (SWIFT MT700) will cover documentary risk. Within the EEA, SEPA Credit Transfers and SEPA Instant Credit Transfers are the lowest-cost standard rails. For imports from tea-producing jurisdictions (e.g., Japan, China, India, Taiwan), the bank may require invoices, packing lists, certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificates, and transport documents; for LC settlements, full set of clean on board bills of lading, commercial invoice, insurance certificate, and beneficiary drafts must be presented within the LC expiry. FX conversion is executed at the bank's spot rate; no prior license is required, but the underlying import documents must be kept for six years for AML/CFT and indirect tax compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/JPY, EUR/CNH, EUR/GBP) for locking import costs on tea and ceramic shipments
FX swaps (swap de change) for temporary liquidity bridging between EUR and soft-currency inbound receipts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies without full convertibility, where permitted by the bank's risk policy and underlying trade documentation
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-term shareholder loans or capital repayment in foreign currency
Vanilla FX options (call/spread) purchased over-the-counter from a Luxembourg authorised credit institution, subject to IFRS hedge accounting and CSSF suitability rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and approval by shareholders (annual general meeting) with filing at the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Account approval by shareholders within 6 months after financial year-end; filing with RCS within 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 2,000; repeated violations may trigger court-imposed fines; persistent non-filing may lead to judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off after multiple years of default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income/wealth tax declaration (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declared by 31 May of the following tax year; extensions are generally available upon written request, with final extended deadline commonly 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; late-filing penalties up to EUR 50,000 under Luxembourg General Tax Law; continued non-compliance may result in tax enforcement and potential strike-off for structural non-cooperation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value-added tax return and annual recapitulative statement (where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg VAT Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT returns due on the 15th day of the month following the reporting period; annual VAT return and European recapitulative statement due no later than 31 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-file interest at 0.6% per month; penalties up to EUR 25,000 for serious or repeated non-compliance; cash seizure and enforced collection initiated after formal demand remains unpaid

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual minimum net wealth tax payment and declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Net Wealth Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual minimum net wealth tax (EUR 500) is due with the net wealth tax declaration, typically aligned with the annual direct tax return filed by 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic default interest assessed at 0.6% per month; enforced collection and distraint upon continued non-payment; failure to maintain filing continuity may be cited in judicial dissolution proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit required for SARL if at financial year-end it exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; average headcount above 50. Exemption is lost if any two are exceeded. Audit also mandatory for listed, public-interest, and certain regulated companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg accounting standards under the Commercial Code); IFRS permissible for consolidated financial statements or for entities that voluntarily adopt IFRS within legal limits

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing for all entities. A SARL must file beneficial-owner details with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) within 30 days after any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership, providing the required supporting documents. Annual confirmation is only triggered by a change, not by calendar rhythm.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges on Ownership Units
Register of Ownership Transfers and Buy-Backs

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Annual fee range for registered office or corporate agent services: USD 1,200 to USD 3,000
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typical certified audit fee range: USD 2,500 to USD 8,000 for a small-to-mid-size SARL
